newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Trial of Rwandan genocide suspect postponed.
newsitem.headline: Trial of Rwandan genocide suspect postponed.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda on Wednesay agreed to postpone until next March the start of trial against a Rwandan Hutu accused of genocide and crimes against humanity, ruling that he was too sick to stand trial next month.
But the three-judge tribunal turned down a defence request to provisionally free the defendant, Georges Rutaganda, saying a sufficient case had not been made for his release.
"The tribunal decides that the date of the beginning of the trial of Georges Anderson Rutaganda is postponed to March 6, 1997," said the presiding judge.
He added that the tribunal "decides that a sufficient case...has not been made out on both a legal and practical basis for the immediate provisional release of Georges Rutaganda."
The tribunal noted that since being transferred to its headquarters in Arusha, Tanzania, Rutaganda had been seriously ill but was given medical care and transferred to a civilian hospital.
Rutaganda did not appear in court during Wednesday's session at the request of his Belgian defence lawyer Luc de Temmerman.
The tribunal was convening for the first time since May to consider De Temmerman's request that Rutaganda be set free on medical grounds.
The tribunal was created by the United Nations after the genocide in Rwanda between April and June 1994, when up to one million minority Tutsis and pro-opposition Hutus were killed.

The killings broke out in the tiny country after the assassination of Hutu president Juvenal Habyarimana on April 6, 1994. Angry followers including the army, militia and Hutu civilians, hunted down Tutsis -- blamed for Habyarimana's death -- and Hutus opposed to his military rule.
The tribunal has a mandate to try only the top planners and perpetrators of the genocide.
The tribunal, which has yet to begin trials, has indicted 21 people and is holding three in custody. They face a maximum penalty of life imprisonment if found guilty.

The tribunal is supposed to begin its first trial on Thursday against Jean Paul Akayesu, 43, also accused of genocide. Akayesu's lawyers have sought an adjournment on procedural and other grounds. That request will be heard on Thursday.
